messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Detected realtime p99 latency spike on /v1/generate (hosted). p95 up 2.1x, p99 up 4.7x vs baseline. Alerting oncall. dashboard: <https://dash.redwood.local/alerts/1789993333>

oncall-lead: I'm on it. pulling up the realtime graphs now. any customer impact flags yet?

sre: Seeing streaming stall spikes in the tail. A subset of streaming requests are hitting >3s per-token stalls, causing p99 to blow up. Error rate stable, but stream disconnects increased ~0.7%.

eng-runtime: Noted increases in KV cache miss ratio for long-context sessions. Also one of the new kernel variants rolled earlier today on a subset of capacity — checking rollout state.

prod-ops: Customer ops flagged two paying customers reporting slow responses in chat windows. They say partial responses then reconnects. Ticketing: INC-4287.

oncall-lead: Ok quick triage checklist: 1) confirm scope (hosts/region/model) 2) check recent deploys/rollouts 3) temporary mitigation (route/scale/fallback) 4) page escalation if customer-impacting.

eng-runtime: Quick results: spike localized to region eu-west-1; model-family: opt-13b-quant and variants. CPU on the serving proxies in that region normal, but GPU worker queue depth has spikes. Kernel rollout ID krl-20260314-09 shows partially active on fleet-a; reverting rollout might be needed.

incident-bot: Deploybot: Rollout krl-20260314-09 started 2026-03-14T09:12Z -> 20% complete.

oncall-lead: Thanks. @eng-runtime, can you pause that kernel rollout? If it's the cause we want quick rollback.

eng-runtime: pausing now...

eng-runtime: paused rollout krl-20260314-09 at 26%. Gate logs: some nodes reported CUDA driver OOM warnings immediately prior to latency spikes.

sre: Correlating traces: requests that hit worker-group A show large enqueue latency at the worker queue; sample trace: ```enqueue 120ms -> worker-schedule 0ms -> kvcache-miss -> kernel-compile 1.4s -> token-gen 2.3s``` That kernel-compile pause looks suspicious (new kernel JIT warmup).

eng-runtime: That matches: new kernel path triggers JIT on first hot requests; compilation showed up as ~1.2-1.6s per process on some GPUs, driving p99. We should disable JIT on that kernel variant for now and fallback to stable kernels.

oncall-lead: Short mitigation options: A) route traffic to stable kernel variant (fast) B) force warmup across pool (slow + traffic cost) C) scale up capacity (costly) D) enable request-level fallback to smaller model for streaming. Thoughts?

prod-ops: For customers currently mid-session, routing changes may cause reconnects. We should prioritize minimizing reconnections but reduce stall severity. Suggest A + D for immediate action.

eng-runtime: Implementing routing rule: in eu-west-1 route /v1/generate streaming to kernel-stable-v1 for 100% on capacity group X. Pushing now.

incident-bot: Router: routing rule applied to region eu-west-1 for path /v1/generate -> kernel-stable-v1. Change id rr-1789993333.

sre: After routing change: p95 back to ~1.3x baseline, p99 starting to come down. Streaming stall rate down from 2.1% to 0.5% in 90s.

customer-ops: Notified affected customers with a proactive message: "We're investigating intermittent slow responses; mitigation in progress." Received acknowledgement from two customers (trial & enterprise).

oncall-lead: Good. Next: full rollback of krl-20260314-09 from fleet-a? eng-runtime, do we need a rollback or can we reconfigure kernel to disable JIT?

eng-runtime: Rollback more reliable. Initiating rollback now to fleet snapshot before rollout. Starting job rb-1789993333. ETA ~2m.

incident-bot: Deploybot: Rollback rb-1789993333 started.

sre: Monitoring tail latency heatmap: still some residual high-percentile tails for long-context (>1024 tokens) sessions; could be KV cache cold starts. Propose warmup script to pre-populate KV for high-volume sessions after rollback completes.

eng-runtime: Rollback finished. krl-20260314-09 fully reverted on fleet-a. Observability: kernel compile times back to normal.

sre: p99 now trending down to 1.6x baseline. streaming disconnects trending back to baseline. We'll watch for 15m.

prod-ops: Recommend keeping routing rule active for +10m then gradually remove. Also file a follow-up action: regression ticket ENG-REG-314 to investigate launch gating and canary thresholds for kernel JITs.

customer-ops: Customers confirmed improved responsiveness. One asked for root cause summary — will prepare a short blurb after RCA.

oncall-lead: Sending oncall handoff: @sre will continue monitoring for the next rotation; if p99 stays within 1.2x baseline after 15m, we close incident. If it flares, page oncall-sre and eng-runtime immediately.

sre: I'll keep a 1h watch. Adding a realtime alert: if p99 > 2x baseline for 5m, page oncall. Alert id: alert-1789993333.

eng-runtime: Action items recorded: 1) ENG-REG-314 (investigate JIT gating + safe defaults) 2) Add kernel warmup path for new kernel rollouts 3) Improve rollout throttles to abort on p99 regressions within 15m

prod-ops: Scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident closed (manual) by oncall-lead. Final notes: partial customer impact for ~9 minutes, root cause: kernel JIT compile causing per-request pauses on first hot paths, mitigated by rollback and routing to stable kernel.

customer-ops: Drafted customer note and sent to affected account owners for review.

oncall-lead: Thanks team. Great quick coordination. If anyone sees residual anomalies, DM me or reopen thread. :thumbsup:
